intro: China is a huge country with 56 officially recognized ethnic groups and many regional languages. Its martial arts grew the same way: as many styles, kept by families, villages, temples, armies and clubs. A Ming general listed many boxing styles around 1560. A national survey in the 1980s recorded well over a hundred.

In this unit you will meet real places and records: the Shaolin Monastery in Henan, the Chen family village, the Jingwu Association of 1910 and the Central Guoshu Institute of 1928. You will see how the People's Republic turned martial arts into wushu, a sport with two codes, taolu and sanda. Then you will follow Chinese arts onto film screens in Hong Kong and the United States.

By the end, you will be able to tell a legend from a record and a film name from a school name. You will be able to name a style by its place, its lineage and its governing body, instead of one English word.
bigQuestion: Why is it more accurate to speak of many Chinese martial arts than of one thing called kung fu?

timeline.t: Shaolin Monastery founded on Mount Song, Henan
A Shaolin stele records the monks' help to Li Shimin around 621
Qi Jiguang lists many boxing styles in the Jixiao Xinshu
Huang Zongxi writes of an internal school set against Shaolin
The Boxer Uprising in northern China
Jingwu Athletic Association opens in Shanghai
Central Guoshu Institute founded in Nanjing
People's Republic founded; first Wong Fei-hung film by Kwan Tak-hing
China adopts the pinyin spelling system
Bruce Lee's four starring films make kung fu a world word
UNESCO lists taijiquan as Intangible Cultural Heritage

words.d: one named martial art system with its own teachers, forms and history
a line of teachers and students who pass an art down over generations
a traditional story about the past that may not be supported by records
an upright stone slab carved with writing, often to record an event
a label from the 1600s for arts linked to Wudang, set against Shaolin's external arts
national art; the Republic of China's name for martial arts from 1928
martial art; the People's Republic of China's name for martial arts and its sport
a wushu event in which one athlete performs a set routine for judges
a wushu event in which two athletes compete under timed rules; also called sanshou
a complete set of rules for one sport or event
martial hero; a Chinese genre of stories set in the distant past
a system for writing words from another script in English letters

test.q: Around 1560, who listed many named boxing styles in a military manual?
test.why: Qi Jiguang's Jixiao Xinshu lists many boxing styles of the Ming period.

test.q: Which province is home to the Shaolin Monastery?
test.why: Shaolin stands on Mount Song near Dengfeng, Henan.

test.q: What kind of evidence is the Shaolin stele of 728?
choices: A historical record carved in stone
test.why: The stele is a record from the Tang period about the monks' help to Li Shimin.

test.q: The Yijin Jing, which claims Bodhidharma as its author, dates from which century?
test.why: Historians date it to the 1600s, so the Bodhidharma link is treated as legend.

test.q: Taijiquan's documented history begins in which place?
choices: Chenjiagou, the Chen family village in Henan
test.why: The Chen family village is the documented starting point; the Zhang Sanfeng story is a legend.

test.q: What did the Jingwu Association, founded in 1910, do differently from family styles?
choices: It taught only one secret style
It taught several styles as a modern club
test.why: Jingwu taught several styles side by side, with members and written rules.

test.q: Which body did the Nationalist government found in Nanjing in 1928?
test.why: The Central Guoshu Institute spread guoshu, the national art.

test.q: What happened to many traditional teachers during the Cultural Revolution (1966–1976)?
choices: They were attacked and some stopped teaching in public
test.why: Old styles were often called feudal, and many teachers were attacked.

test.q: Which pair of wushu events are two different codes under the IWUF?
test.why: Taolu scores a solo routine; sanda sets two athletes against each other.

test.q: What was wushu's status at the 2008 Beijing Olympics?
choices: A special tournament with no official Olympic medals
test.why: Wushu had an IOC-approved tournament but was not an official medal sport.

test.q: Why does English often use Cantonese names like Wing Chun?
choices: Many teachers who went abroad spoke Cantonese
Films were only made in Mandarin
test.why: Many southern teachers came from Guangdong and Hong Kong, where Cantonese is spoken.

test.q: Which U.S. law ended the old national immigration quotas?
choices: The Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965
test.why: The 1965 act opened immigration more widely, and more teachers arrived.

test.q: Which real teacher taught Bruce Lee Wing Chun and later became a film hero himself?
test.why: Ip Man taught in Hong Kong from the 1950s; the film Ip Man came out in 2008.

test.q: In Fist of Fury (1972), which element is invented?
test.why: Chen Zhen is fictional; the school, the city and Huo Yuanjia are real.

test.q: Why is The Karate Kid (2010) a good example of names traveling apart from what they name?
choices: It kept a karate title while showing Chinese arts in Beijing
It was made by the IWUF
test.why: The studio kept the famous title as a brand, though the story moved to Beijing.

write.prompt: Is it more accurate to call Chinese martial arts one thing, kung fu, or many things? Argue your answer using at least three records from this unit, such as the Jixiao Xinshu (c. 1560), Huang Zongxi's epitaph (1669), the Central Guoshu Institute (1928) or the IWUF codes for taolu and sanda.
tips: Name each record and give its date.
Label legends as legends and records as records.
Name styles by their place, such as Chen style taijiquan from Henan.
Compare film names with school names instead of judging either.
Use unit words such as lineage, code, guoshu and wushu.
